summary: End-to-end verification of the TACHO DEDUP BUG FIX plus 3 new features (Tacho Portal tabs/grouping, Calendar custom events, Insurance folder filter). Added TestTachoDedupBug (2 tests) and TestCalendarEvents (3 tests) to /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py. Ran the new tests together with regression TestTacho (6) + TestInsurance (1) — 13/13 PASSED in 8.9s. Bug fix confirmed on the LIVE dashboard: created 3 tacho records for the same driver (Driver Card, reference='Dedup Driver Test') with last_download 120d/60d/2d ago; /api/dashboard returned exactly ONE alert for that driver with status='due_soon' (days=26) — NOT expired — and counts.tacho increased by only 1 (distinct references), not 3. counts.expired did NOT increment (before=6, after=6), i.e. the older records are ignored. Also verified in /api/calendar: only ONE tacho event surfaces per (source_type, reference), dated to the latest next_due (today+26d, due_soon). Frontend (Playwright, 1920x1080): logged in as manager@haulcheck.co.uk. /tacho page shows the two tabs (tacho-tab-drivers / tacho-tab-vehicles), records grouped by reference, latest surfaced as the card headline, older 2 downloads collapsed under a '2 earlier downloads' expander. Switching to Vehicle Units tab shows 0 cards for the driver-card test (isolation good). /calendar: Add Event button (cal-add-event) opens the dialog with event-date prefilled to the selected day; saving via save-event-button persists the event via POST /api/calendar/events and it appears in the day-detail panel with the Flag icon and 'Event' label. delete-event-button removes it (verified backend 200 + 'Event removed' toast). /insurance: with policies seeded for Motor — Truck + Goods in Transit (GIT), the insurance-folders row renders all 8 buttons (folder-All / folder-Truck / folder-Trailer / folder-GIT / folder-PL / folder-EL / folder-Green Card / folder-Other) with counts; clicking folder-Truck filters to Motor — Truck cards only, folder-GIT filters to GIT only, folder-All restores everything. Regression smoke: tacho CRUD + Log Download + dropdown + auto-read intact (from iteration 10 tests + TestTacho suite). Logout via logout-button returns to /login. All 13 backend tests PASSED; frontend E2E flows all PASSED. Cleaned up all TEST_ data via API (3 tacho, 1 driver, 2 insurance, 1 calendar event).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py gather_stats (line 1242) and calendar (line 1109): dedup logic uses lexicographic string comparison on ISO dates via `(tc.get('last_download') or tc.get('next_due') or '')` — this is safe for YYYY-MM-DD ISO dates but subtle. Records without any date will collide with each other under empty-string ordering; if two records for the same reference both have no dates, only one is kept arbitrarily. Fine in practice since a tacho record without last_download/next_due is a data-entry error.
server.py line 1247 dedup key uses (source_type, reference) — Driver Card + name and Vehicle Unit + registration are separate keys, correct.

server.py POST /api/calendar/events (line 1140) does NOT validate the `date` string is a real ISO date — an invalid string like 'not-a-date' will still be inserted and later ignored by the calendar-day filter. Low priority; consider `datetime.fromisoformat(data.date)` for defensiveness.

server.py DELETE /api/calendar/events/{eid} returns {ok:true} even when nothing matched (no 404). Minor consistency issue vs other DELETE endpoints (e.g. /tacho, /vehicles) which are also silent. Existing pattern, not a regression.
Tacho.js line 82 grouped() sorts by `last_download || next_due` descending — matches backend dedup logic exactly, so the FE 'latest' card and backend alert status will always agree.
Calendar.js line 41 openAddEvent() prefills date to `selected`, and line 187 uses type=date input — good UX, works with both HTML5 date picker and manual entry.

Insurance.js line 40 FOLDERS array uses the exact `policy_type` string that the backend returns/expects (`Motor — Truck` with em-dash). Any drift in that string on the backend would silently break the Truck filter. Consider deriving from a shared constant.
Insurance.js line 100 `items.length > 0` gates the folders row — user with 0 policies sees NO folder row. Acceptable UX; could still render disabled folders for discoverability.

success_rate.backend: 100% (13/13 tests passed for dedup + calendar events + tacho + insurance regression)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (login, dashboard dedup, tacho tabs/grouping, calendar add/delete event, insurance folder filter, logout — all verified)

seed_data_creation: Test run created 3 tacho records + 1 driver ('Dedup Driver Test') + 2 insurance policies + 1 calendar event; ALL deleted via API afterwards. Backend TestTachoDedupBug + TestCalendarEvents fixtures also self-clean.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug (tacho dedup) is fixed and verified end-to-end. Key change locations in /app/backend/server.py: gather_stats() dedupes tacho by (source_type, reference) taking the record with max last_download (or next_due) before computing expired/due_soon and counts (counts.tacho = number of DISTINCT keys). calendar() does the same dedup for the calendar events. NEW endpoints POST /api/calendar/events + DELETE /api/calendar/events/{id} (calendar_events collection). Frontend selectors added: tacho-tab-drivers, tacho-tab-vehicles, cal-add-event, event-date, event-title, event-notes, save-event-button, delete-event-button, insurance-folders, folder-<label>. Existing manager account has 1 seeded tacho (John Smith) plus PMI/insurance/defect seed data from prior iterations. Login must use data-testid='submit-auth-button' (there are TWO buttons with text 'Sign In' — the tab-login pill and the submit button).
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: gather_stats() previously iterated over ALL tacho records for a user and evaluated compliance_status on each row's next_due. A user's single driver card that had been downloaded weekly for months would surface DOZENS of 'expired' rows because every historical row had next_due = old_download + 28 days (all in the past). Each old row contributed a 25-point penalty to the compliance score AND its own alert entry, tanking the dashboard to 0/100 even when the driver was fully in-date. FIX: build tacho_latest dict keyed by (source_type, reference), keeping the record with the max last_download; iterate only over tacho_latest.values() for alert generation and counts. Verified: creating 3 records (120d/60d/2d ago) now produces exactly 1 alert (status=due_soon, 26d) and counts.tacho counts distinct refs, not raw records. Regression risk: none — the change is confined to gather_stats() + calendar() aggregation; underlying /api/tacho CRUD is untouched, historical records are preserved so the Tacho Portal grouping UI can still show them under 'earlier downloads'.
